breaking_changes.BC_description: Node.js support has been dropped for versions earlier than 18.19.0 and versions between 20.0.0 and 20.4.0.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Upgrade Node.js to version 18.19.0 or higher, or if using version 20, upgrade to at least version 20.5.0.

breaking_changes.BC_description: When the encoding option is set to 'buffer', the output (result.stdout, result.stderr, result.all) now returns a Uint8Array instead of a Buffer. The encoding: null option has also been removed.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method:
Update code that expects Buffer instances to work with Uint8Array instead. Buffer methods will need to be replaced with Uint8Array equivalents or you can convert Uint8Array to Buffer using Buffer.from() if needed.

Before:
```js
const {stdout} = await execa('node', ['file.js'], {encoding: 'buffer'});
console.log(stdout instanceof Buffer); // true
```

After:
```js
const {stdout} = await execa('node', ['file.js'], {encoding: 'buffer'});
console.log(stdout instanceof Uint8Array); // true
// If Buffer is needed:
const stdoutBuffer = Buffer.from(stdout);
```

Also note that the `encoding: null` option has been removed. Use `encoding: 'buffer'` instead.

breaking_changes.BC_description: Several encoding option values have been renamed in the execa library, including: null to 'buffer', 'utf-8' to 'utf8', 'UTF8' to 'utf8', 'utf-16le' to 'utf16le', 'ucs2' to 'utf16le', 'ucs-2' to 'utf16le', and 'binary' to 'latin1'. Additionally, the 'buffer' encoding now returns a Uint8Array instead of a Buffer, and 'encoding: null' has been removed entirely.

The methods for piping output to files (subprocess.pipeStdout(), subprocess.pipeStderr(), and subprocess.pipeAll()) have been removed. Instead, the file path should be provided as an object with a 'file' property to the stdout or stderr option.

The methods for piping output to writable streams (subprocess.pipeStdout(), subprocess.pipeStderr(), and subprocess.pipeAll()) have been removed. Instead, the stream should be passed directly to the stdout or stderr option, or as ['pipe', stream] if the stream does not have a file descriptor.

The subprocess.pipeStdout(), subprocess.pipeStderr(), and subprocess.pipeAll() methods have been renamed to subprocess.pipe(). The command and arguments can now be passed directly to subprocess.pipe() without calling execa() again. The 'from' option can specify the source stream ('stdout', 'stderr', or 'all').
The 'signal' option in execa methods has been renamed to 'cancelSignal'. Passing the old 'signal' option now throws an error.

In the execa library, the `error.killed` property has been renamed to `error.isTerminated`. This property indicates whether the process was terminated/killed. Note that on Windows, this property has partial support due to differences in how process termination is handled compared to Unix-based systems.
The subprocess.cancel() method has been removed from the execa library. Use subprocess.kill() or the cancelSignal option instead.

The forceKillAfterTimeout option has been renamed to forceKillAfterDelay, and is now passed to execa() instead of to subprocess.kill(). This option, which controls the time to wait before forcefully killing a process, has been moved from the kill() method to the top-level execa() options.
The verbose option in the execa library has changed from a boolean to a string enum. The value false has been renamed to 'none' and true has been renamed to 'short'.
The execPath option has been renamed to nodePath. It is now a noop unless the node option is true. It now works even if the preferLocal option is false.

The default serialization option is now 'advanced' instead of 'json'. When calling subprocess.send(object) with an object that contains functions or symbols, those were previously silently removed. Now this will throw an exception.

If subprocess.stdout, subprocess.stderr or subprocess.all is manually piped, the .pipe() call must now happen as soon as subprocess is created. Otherwise, the output at the beginning of the subprocess might be missing.
Signals passed to subprocess.kill() method and to the killSignal option of execa(), execaSync() functions must now be uppercase (e.g., 'SIGTERM') instead of lowercase ('sigterm').
